full_judgment:
3. Mr. S K. Sinha, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the 1earned Magistrate acted in excess of his jurisdiction under section 250B of the Code of Criminal Procedure in holding that the charge against the accused opposite parties is groundless upon taking into consideration the documents which were not produced before the Police during investigation nor the same were submitted by the Investigating Officer to the court along with his report under section 173 of the said Code notwithstanding the fact that the materials on record namely the statement of the witnesses recorded by the police under section 161 of the Code show that there has been strong prima facie specific charge against the accused persons under sections 144/447/379 of the Penal Code and, for the ends of justice, these charges are required to be tried on merit upon the evidence to be adduced by the parties at the trial. The learned Advocate has further submitted that the learned Magistrate has also acted illegally, in a hearing under section 250B of the Code, in holding, that as per F.I.R. and the charge sheet there has been shifting of the place of occurrence and that from the document of both the parties it is evident that there has been dispute between the parties in respect of right title interest and possession in the disputed land and that since the charge-sheet has been submitted against only 3 persons the charge under section 144 of the Penal Code is not maintainable. The learned Advocate has seriously assailed the Judgment in the aforesaid criminal Motion and submitted that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has also misconceived the scope of hearing under section 250R of the said Code, in taking into consideration the patta dated 23.3.56 of the accused opposite parties, in holding that since there is a bona fide dispute regarding possession of the parties over the disputed land, the charge under sections 379/447 of the Penal Code was not sustainable, 

 4. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties has however sought to support the impugned order and submitted, inter alia, that since the accused opposite parties have teen possessing the disputed land on the basis of the registered Patta dated 23.2.56 which they get in pursuance of a decree passed in O. suit No. 51/51, against which the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner filed O.S No. 76765 for setting aside that decree and the same was dismissed on contest the courts below did not commit any illegality in taking into consideration these judgments and decrees and the relevant registered patta in a hearing under section 2508 of the said Code, inasmuch as these documents prima facie show that the accused persons have been possessing the disputed land since long before the alleged date of occurrence. 

 5. It appears from the orders of the Courts below and from the records that the petitioner has been claiming right title and possession over the disputed land on the basis of three registered Kabalas of the years 1972 and 1973 and the accused opposite parties have also been claiming their title and possession over the name on the basis of the registered patta of the year 1956. During investigation the police did not seize those documents of the parties and the parties themselves of their own accord produced these documents before the Magistrate in hearing under section 250B of the Code. 

 12. It is also evident that the learned Magistrate without considering the documents sent along with charge-sheet i.e. the statements of the witness recorded by the Investigation officer during investigation and upon consideration of the documents, produced by the parties at the time of hearing the case under section 250B Cr.P.C. has found that there having been dispute between the parties over right, title, interest and possession in the "disputed land, no prima facie case has been made out against the accused under sections 447/379 B.P.C. also. These documents viz, pattas and kabalas of e parties cannot prove that there was criminal trespass and theft in respect of the disputed land on 6.11.80, The documents which have been referred to in the impugned order simply show that there is a claim and a counter-claim regarding the title by the parties over the disputed land. Thus, it is abundantly clear that the learned Magistrate acted illegally and in excess of his jurisdiction in discharging the accused persons under section 250 B of the Code of Criminal Procedure which has caused miscarriage of justice.
